Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). text: Bean yellow mosaic virus disease is caused by a Mosaic-group virus and can produce severe symptoms from an early growth stage, stunting plant development. It is transmitted by piercing-sucking insect vectors including thrips, leafhoppers ("hoppers"), and aphids. Symptoms include yellow mottling on leaves and abnormal curling of pods, described in the source as "pod curl." Widespread infection can severely reduce mung bean yield. Prevention/control measures listed: use tolerant/resistant varieties where available; time planting to break the pest/host cycle; use appropriate plant spacing; source disease-free seed; and, most importantly, rogue out and destroy infected plants as soon as they are detected to limit spread. Because spread depends on insect vectors, controlling those insects is central to managing this disease; active ingredients named for that purpose include Thiamethoxam, Buprofezin, Dinotefuran, Imidacloprid, Nitenpyram, Acetamiprid, Pymetrozine, and Fenobucarb.
